newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil allows creation of new coffee council.
newsitem.headline: Brazil allows creation of new coffee council.

text.p: The Brazilian government Friday published a decree allowing for the creation of a new coffee policy council, a spokeswoman for the Presidency said.
"The government has allowed (through the decree) for the creation of the Deliberative Council for Coffee Policy (CDPC) under the auspices of the Ministry of Industry and Commerce," she told Reuters.
In a decree setting out the structure and functions of the entire government, Brasilia quietly altered the number of departments in the Ministry of Industry and Commerce by adding the council.
The Presidency spokeswoman said the council itself had still to be created through a separate law.
The new council is expected to include both private and public sector representatives and will decide future Brazilian coffee policy.
Its creation was suggested by a parliamentary committee and the private sector, which has long complained that Brazilian coffee policy lacked clarity and focus.
A spokeswoman for the Ministry of Industry and Commerce said the primary commodities department could not immediately confirm that the legal framework had been set up for the creation of the CDPC.
